content.text: No renewal or term-extension mechanic exists in the agreement, so the risk this rule targets is absent.

input.quote: 2. TERM. The term of this Agreement shall begin on the date hereof and shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6 hereof.
input.rationale: The Agreement has no auto-renewal mechanic at all: the term runs from signature until terminated (p0011), and under § 6(a) either party may terminate for convenience on fifteen (15) days' notice whenever no Statement of Work is outstanding (p0032). There is therefore no renewal term to compute, no non-renewal notice window (and so nothing approaching the 30/60/90-day thresholds), and no automatic multi-year renewal. Commitment arises only if we affirmatively sign a new Statement of Work, which is equivalent to the preferred position of renewal by mutual written agreement, and the exit right is shorter than the preferred 30 days' notice. No redline is warranted; the structure is more favourable to us than the preferred position. One adjacent observation, not a deviation under this rule: § 3(b) lets Contractor "change rates with 30 days notice to Company" without a CPI/percentage cap (p0014). That is a mid-term pricing right rather than a renewal uplift, so it belongs to the pricing/rate-increase rule; it is mitigated here because rates are fixed per Statement of Work and we can terminate on fifteen days' notice, but the pricing reviewer may wish to add a cap.
